title: 2-D disk plane-shear cell: is the 16-57 % mu(I) offset a dimensional artefact?
written_at: before the analysis of cluster job cj4011 (the probe and the production sweep were queued when this file was written; no run artifact existed)
question: Rounds 1-23 measured mu(I) on 3-D spheres and judged it against the 2-D disk law of da Cruz et al. 2005. Round 23 closed the seed hypothesis (CV up to 20.6 %) and left exactly one candidate mechanism for the +29 % offset at I = 0.03: dimension. This round measures the law on a device of the law's own dimension: monodisperse 2-D disks, rough (grain-glued) walls, constant confining stress, prescribed shear rate.

reference.source: da Cruz, Emam, Prochnow, Roux, Chevoir 2005 Phys. Rev. E 72:021309, Eq. (13)-(14)
reference.mu_law: mu(I) = mu_min + b I, valid for I <= I_saturation
reference.phi_law: phi(I) = nu_max - a I, valid for I <= I_saturation
reference.note: I > 0.2 is outside the fit; DaCruzLaw.mu() returns None there and such points are reported, never judged.

device.kind: 2-D monodisperse disks, periodic in x, two pinned rows of glued grains as rough walls
device.cell: W = 0.40 m (40 d) x gap = 0.30 m (30 d), ~1220 free disks
device.protocol: compaction at constant P with the rows held still (40-60 d/sqrt(P/rho)), then shear through 0.5 strain of transient, then a measurement window of 1.0 strain
device.primary_mu_ordinate: mu_wall: the two pinned rows carry equal and opposite tractions, so each row is summed separately and the pair averaged; because the wall grains are particles, no wall load is lost and no wall-slip law is assumed (the walls are rough by construction)
device.secondary_mu_ordinate: mu_bulk: symmetric part of the Love-Weber tensor over all contacts / (W h_eff t); reported as a consistency check, NOT the judging ordinate, because in 2-D the friction contacts carry a contact couple that the symmetric virial does not include
device.primary_phi_ordinate: phi_gap = free-disk area / (W h_eff), h_eff = wall-grain surface-to-surface distance (the pinned rows carry no free volume, so the control volume of the sheared material is surface-to-surface). phi_cell (centre-to-centre, half wall layers included) is reported as the secondary definition.
device.measured_ordinates_for_I: I = gammadot_measured d / sqrt(p/rho) with gammadot_measured = 2 V / h_eff and p the measured confining stress

tolerance.basis: the ledger acceptance (<10 % vs the archived law) -- unchanged, not relaxed

P1.statement: estimator calibration: at every judged point the wall traction and the virial agree with the imposed stress, |p_wall/P - 1| <= 0.10 and |sigma_yy/P - 1| <= 0.10

P2.statement: dimensionality: the 2-D device lands inside the 10 % band of the archived 2-D law at every judged point

P3.statement: if dimension is the mechanism, mu_2D is BELOW mu_3D at the same I by more than the 3-D seed spread (relative difference >= 10 % at I = 0.02 and 0.1)
P3.falsified_if: mu_2D is not lower than mu_3D, or the gap is smaller than 10 %, in which case dimension is not the explanation and the residual sits in the device or the estimator

P4.statement: phi: phi_gap is inside the 10 % band of nu_max - a I at every judged point, i.e. the round-22 WITHHELD verdict on phi is resolved by making the definition commensurable

P5.statement: stationarity: |drift_z(mu_wall)| < 2 between the two halves of the measurement window at every judged point and seed

decision_rule.acceptance: PASS iff every judged point (I <= I_saturation) is within 10 % of the archived law on mu; phi judged separately
decision_rule.if_fail: report the sign and size of the residual against the 3-D device at the same I; a residual much smaller than the 3-D one confirms dimension as a contributor, an unchanged residual falsifies it
decision_rule.honest_fail: a failing outcome is published as FAIL with the same detail as a passing one; no tolerance is re-negotiated after the fact
